`voyage-4-large` is Voyage AI’s flagship text embedding model in the Voyage 4 family, aimed at high-quality retrieval rather than text generation. It uses a mixture-of-experts architecture, supports a 32K-token context window, and offers embedding sizes of 256, 512, 1024, or 2048 dimensions.[1][2][3]
## What it is
Voyage AI describes `voyage-4-large` as its top-performing general-purpose and multilingual embedding model, and says the Voyage 4 series shares a compatible embedding space across `voyage-4-large`, `voyage-4`, and `voyage-4-lite`. That means you can mix models within the same retrieval pipeline for different cost and latency tradeoffs without changing embedding compatibility.[1][3]
## Main specs
The model supports a 32,000-token context length and multiple output dimensions, with 1024 as the default in Voyage’s documentation. Several sources also note support for quantization options and Matryoshka-style dimension reduction, which helps when you want smaller vectors without fully retraining your system.[4][5][3]
## Why people use it
Its main use case is semantic search, retrieval, and RAG systems where the quality of document and query matching matters more than generation. Voyage AI says `voyage-4-large` is the strongest model in the series for retrieval quality, while third-party listings repeat that it is designed for the best general-purpose and multilingual retrieval performance.[1][6][3]
## Performance positioning
Voyage AI states that `voyage-4-large` is the first production embedding model in this family to use mixture-of-experts, and says this lets it deliver frontier-level retrieval accuracy with lower serving cost than comparable dense models. Their launch materials and related marketplace pages report about 40% lower serving costs than comparable dense alternatives, while a MongoDB technical post discusses a 75% reduction in active parameters with nearly the same retrieval accuracy as dense models.[1][2][7]
## Pricing note
One recent pricing aggregator lists `voyage-4-large` starting at $0.12 per 1M input tokens, but pricing can vary by provider and may change over time. For production decisions, it is better to verify against the current Voyage API or your serving platform’s billing page.[8]
